name: integration-tests
$tagsComment: `scope:shared` was here alongside `type:integration-test`. Nx permits a dependency when ANY tag matches, so `scope:shared` let any feature library import a harness that issues `DELETE /nuxeo/api/v1/path/...` and `Document.Trash`, while `type:integration-test` appeared in no rule in `eslint.config.mjs` and governed nothing. The single tag is now the only one, and `eslint.config.mjs` names it as a source but never as a permitted target — so this library may read the platform it drives and nothing may depend on it. Verified by importing it from a feature library and watching lint reject the edge.
// targets: to see all targets run: nx show project integration-tests --web

test.$comment: The unit half only, and it cannot become anything else: `vitest.unit.config.mts` includes `*.unit.spec.ts` and the `integration` target's config includes `*.integration.spec.ts`, so no file can match both. What runs here is the preflight's decision logic and the CLI's exit-code mapping with `fetch` stubbed — no Nuxeo, no Angular, nothing that a CI runner lacks.
test.$whyComment: The `integration` target does not run on CI, so until this existed the gate that decides whether the whole suite may run was itself unexercised there, and its exit-2-versus-exit-1 behaviour rested on one manual observation. A one-character edit could have collapsed the two codes with nothing going red.

integration.$comment: Named `integration`, not `test`, so no `-t test` invocation can reach the specs it runs. Those require a live Nuxeo; CI runners have none, so `nx affected -t test` and `nx run-many -t test` would fail every one of them on a precondition. An exclusion list in each workflow would work only for as long as everyone remembers to extend it — the name cannot be forgotten. The `test` target added beside this one does not weaken that: the two configs select on disjoint filename patterns, so a live spec has to be renamed before `-t test` can see it, and a rename is visible in a diff.
integration.$preflightComment: Preflight first, so an absent or empty Nuxeo — or a target host that is not allowed — reports as a precondition rather than as sixty-odd product failures. Same shape as nuxeo-ui-e2e's `e2e`. Note that `nx` normalises a failed command to exit 1, so the preflight's exit 2 does NOT survive `nx run integration-tests:integration` — `npm run beta:integration` chains the same two commands with `&&` and does preserve it. That is why both exist, exactly as `beta:e2e` exists beside `nuxeo-ui-e2e:e2e`.
integration.$allowlistComment: This target needs `NUXEO_USER`, `NUXEO_PASS` and `INTEGRATION_ALLOWED_HOSTS` in the environment. The last one is the run-safety gate and it denies by default: a host it does not name is refused with exit 2, `localhost` included, because the guard it replaced compared the credentials against the Docker default and so recorded every real production pair as satisfying it. It is read from the environment only — no flag, no per-suite option — so nothing in this repository can relax it on the caller's behalf. See libs/integration-tests/README.md.
integration.$cacheComment: Deliberately NOT cached: the result depends on a live Nuxeo's contents, and a cached green would assert something about a server state that has since changed.

typecheck.$comment: `preflight-cli.ts` is neither a spec nor part of any bundle, so `spec-typecheck.mjs` does not reach it and there is no `build` target that would. Without this target the one file in the repository whose job is to exit with the right code would be the one file nothing type-checks.

$testTargetHistory: This project deliberately had NO `test` target, so that the live specs could not be reached by `-t test`. That reasoning survives — see the two targets above — but the blanket version of it had a cost that was not noticed until SonarCloud reported 0% coverage on the new code: `scripts/beta-harness/coverage-gate.mjs` discovers projects by the presence of `targets.test`, so the library was outside the ratchet entirely, and the preflight and its CLI were measured by nothing. The narrow `test` target puts only the server-free half in that population. `integration-preflight.unit.spec.ts` imports `assertUntruncated` and related helpers from `integration-harness.ts`, so the harness is partially covered without mocking live DELETEs. `user-fixtures.ts` is deliberately NOT unit-tested — it issues real DELETEs against a real repository, and a mocked version would assert the mock — so it sits in the report at 0% and drags the project's figure down — measured 41% statements on 2026-09-28, against ~28% when this note was written; the figure moves as the unit half grows, which is why the mechanism below and not the number is the point. That is the honest number and it is meant to be read as debt, not patched away: they need no allowlist entry, because v8 instruments them and they are inside the denominator rather than invisible outside it, which is the state the allowlist exists to record. Re-measured on the pull request after review claimed the opposite — that v8 omits an unimported file rather than reporting it at 0%, so `coverage-gate.mjs` would block. `nx test integration-tests --coverage` lists `user-fixtures.ts` at 0% statements, lines 16-453 uncovered, and the gate passes; `coverage.all` is what put an unimported source file in the denominator under Vitest 3; Vitest 4 removed it and drops such a file from the report, so `coverage.include` in `vitest.unit.config.mts` now does the same job. `nuxeo-ui-e2e` remains in the original position, with no `test` target and no entry.
